newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: DAEWOO TUMBLES AGAIN AFTER PROFIT-WARNING.
newsitem.headline: DAEWOO TUMBLES AGAIN AFTER PROFIT-WARNING.

text.p: Consumer electronics firm Daewoo Electronics South Africa Ltd shares fell again on Wednesday after it issued a profit warning on Tuesday.
At 0949 GMT, it was trading down 56 cents or 24.4 percent at 174 cents on volume of some 320,000 shares.
"It is very definitely (down) on the profit-warning. They are being slaughtered on the back of that," one dealer said.
Daewoo said on Tuesday it would report a significant loss for the half year to June 30 due to tougher-than-expected market conditions.
It blamed high interest rates, delayed purchases of large household electrical goods and a flood of illegal imports.
Dealers said the share price would remain weak.
"It will battle substantially, I don't see much upside from a trading point of view," one dealer said.

The counter traded at a year low of 130 cents on June 4, but recovered to a year high of 330 cents on July 29 in anticipation of better interim results and an offshore cash injection which failed to materialise.
The firm's results will be published later in August.
